label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

passages.starts: For years my slides were a compromise. I had an idea
passages.why: A story I can follow straight away, and it tells me who is talking and what the problem was.

passages.starts: On 29 October I gave a talk where I mostly did not
passages.why: Shows the payoff in plain words (press play, it moves), which makes me want page two.

passages.starts: What gave me that was not a better slide tool. It was a factory:

passages.starts: Online, under each scene, you can open the commits, times and files
passages.why: I do not know what a commit is, and this is logistics about a website, not the story; cut from the page.

passages.starts: The talk of 58 beats, given on the evening of 29 October.

passages.starts: This book is one of a series, Generation ZX Founders (GenAI Edition),
passages.why: The one idea (you start, you build) is welcome, but a series name and a quoted line arrive before I have a reason to care; open with 'this is a book about you doing it'.

passages.starts: Generation ZX is not a range of birth years;
passages.why: Tells me I am welcome and the book is not only for programmers, which settles my worry; 'Faro' needs a few words of explanation.

passages.why: I do not know what a brief is and 'rules' for what; one plain phrase each would help before 'I asked for a team'.

passages.starts: Dev (happy, the fast one): First pass of the site and the talk.
passages.why: Short, characterful speech that makes the agents feel like people at last.

passages.starts: Conductor (pacing): I keep the time. Everyone gets a slot,
passages.why: Clear job in two lines, and 'pull the hold' is planted for later.

passages.starts: Deck (proud, the fussy one): The slides are mine.
passages.why: A clear, funny voice and an obvious job.

passages.starts: ruv-sgit (absorbed, the night owl): I will be in my workshop
passages.why: The name is odd and 'things you can check' is vague; say what this agent makes.

passages.starts: None of it was new. The build, the check, the brief, the hold:

passages.starts: (The cast cards for the four, the designer's scorecards: on stage from,
passages.why: Design instructions about cards and ids in small type mean nothing to me here; keep for the designer, not the reader page.

passages.starts: In the small hours, the conductor built the factory's machinery.
passages.why: Short bridge that tells me where we are in the day.

passages.starts: A clock: each member wakes at its own minute. A hold anyone can pull.
passages.why: 'Wakes' and 'plan, check, do, check, check again' arrive in one breath; give it as a list of five short steps.

passages.starts: It ran the five steps on its own first piece of work,
passages.why: A small, human surprise (it was caught out) that makes the process believable.

passages.starts: Reviewer (a second agent with a checker's brief, drawn as a clipboard):
passages.why: Easy to picture and the quote is plain.

passages.starts: That last line is one of the most honest things anyone on the team wrote.
passages.why: Tells me the limit of the checks honestly, which builds trust.

passages.starts: That is the loop. I could change my mind, and the factory could

passages.why: What was the lock for? A phrase on what it would have protected.

passages.page: Page 8. What did not work (the interview)
passages.starts: The talk needed more rounds than one day gave it. The checks worked,

passages.page: Page 9. The factory, taken apart and rebuilt
passages.starts: Conductor (pacing, to the reader): Same clock. Same hold. More hands on it.

passages.starts: Conductor (straight to the reader): Start with one of me.

passages.starts: You: one tool and one empty project. An account with an AI agent tool

passages.starts: You: one page of rules, in your own words: what the agent is for,
passages.why: Clear and doable with no code.

passages.starts: You: one brief: what you want made, for whom, by when.
passages.why: Clear and doable; the brief is finally defined here, which should happen on page 3.

passages.starts: Your agent builds, you check: something small that somebody else can use,
passages.why: A realistic goal for a student, and it repeats.

passages.starts: Add a second agent only when the first is busy. Working with others?

passages.starts: It does not have to be a talk: a shop's customer answers
passages.why: Shows other uses so I see myself in it.

passages.starts: What it costs: to start, you need a free account; paid plans

if_you_cut_one_page: Page 2 (the series page): it is the only page with no scene, it arrives before I have a reason to care, and its one useful message (this is for you, not only for programmers) could be one sentence at the end of page 1.
notes: Pages 1, 7 and 10 worked for me as a non-coder. Pages 5, 6 and 8 lost me: the quoted lines carry no setup, so I could not tell what the agents were arguing about. Terms like brief, board, hold and gate need a gloss at first use, not a box on page 3. The in-text 'Band' lines and record codes were skipped as instructed but a few sit as visible reader text (the Zoom in line, the dramatised note) and read as team logistics.
